1	# Proposing
2	
3	Two principles (1 and 2 in SKILL.md): **get approval for work that is costly
4	or hard to undo**, and **build so every task is easy to undo**, approved or
5	not. A wrong idea costs a few lines to correct in a
6	proposal and a rewrite once built, so unless the task is easy to reverse
7	and takes little effort to execute, its first reply after its first look is
8	a proposal, and code waits for Approve. The same goes when the user
9	asks what you think, and for a task the queue started: a non-trivial one
10	waits on its card with no one present, as a task waiting on questions does.
11	
12	A proposal is the task's `## Before` and `## After` made into a card: Before
13	and After side by side (see [Showing the change](#showing-the-change)), the
14	one line, and the calls it rests on as questions (see [Questions](questions.md)).
15	Write `## Before` and `## After` in `SPLATES.md` first, then the card from them.
16	
17	**Start low-effort, easily reversible tasks without asking permission.**
18	These tasks need no proposal card or approval before building: a typo, a
19	small fix, or a rename the compiler checks, for example. Judge by execution
20	effort and how easily the result can be undone, rather than line count or
21	whether the change is visible. Say so in one line, such as `Small and easy
22	to revert: building directly.`, then proceed. Ask only when an unresolved
23	choice materially changes the outcome; do not ask whether to start the task.
24	Tasks that take substantial effort or are hard to reverse still need a proposal.
25	
26	A proposal is one block: a `## 💡 Proposed <subject>` title, the subject a
27	few words on what you would build, then what you recommend and why, briefly.
28	It ends with each call it rests on that the user has not settled, as
29	questions numbered from 1 (see [Questions](questions.md)).
30	
31	**Before you write one, decide whether it needs a picture.** Any visible
32	frontend change, and any backend change across several services, tables or
33	flows, is proposed with attached images, never in text alone: capture them
34	first, as [Showing the change](#showing-the-change) says, then write the
35	block. A text description or ASCII sketch does not stand in for them.
36	
37	```markdown
38	## 💡 Proposed a card for proposals
39	
40	Fold proposals into the questions card, each call a question with a pick:
41	that card already tags a `(chosen)` choice, so one card asks everything.
42	
43	1. Where should a proposal's calls come from?
44	   - (a) The reply, so a proposal works outside a task too (chosen)
45	   - (b) `SPLATES.md`, so every proposal needs a task
46	2. What should its button say?
47	```
48	
49	## Showing the change
50	
51	A proposal shows what it would change, in a picture, when the change is
52	big enough to need one: a backend change touching more than one service,
53	table or flow, and any visible frontend change. A small change needs none.
54	
55	- **Backend: a D2 diagram.** Write the `.d2` source (a sequence, flow, data or
56	  state diagram, whichever the change is) in a scratch directory outside the
57	  worktree and render it to SVG. When `d2` is on the PATH (`command -v d2`),
58	  use it: `d2 in.d2 out.svg`. Otherwise use `@terrastruct/d2`, the WASM build
59	  of D2 on npm. It ships no command, and nothing is added to any repository:
60	  write this script beside the source, where Bun installs the import on the
61	  first run and caches it after, and run `bun render-d2.ts in.d2 out.svg`.
62	
63	  ```ts
64	  import { D2 } from "@terrastruct/d2";
65	
66	  const [input, output] = process.argv.slice(2);
67	  const d2 = new D2();
68	  const result = await d2.compile(await Bun.file(input).text());
69	  await Bun.write(output, await d2.render(result.diagram, result.renderOptions));
70	  process.exit(0); // the WASM runtime keeps the process alive otherwise
71	  ```
72	
73	  Cards show attached images, not SVGs, so the SVG becomes a PNG: with `d2`
74	  on the PATH, `d2 in.d2 out.png` renders the PNG directly, no browser
75	  needed; otherwise open the SVG in the browser tool and screenshot it.
76	  A proposal for such a change is not ready until its diagram is attached,
77	  so do not send it as text alone. `splates attach` works from a task's
78	  worktree: when no task is under way, `splates add` one for the proposal
79	  first (After says what is proposed), rather than skipping the picture.
80	  Put the PNG in the proposal under a short heading for what it shows. Keep the sections beside
81	  it in the same order each time (`Flow`, `Data`, `Risks`), each a few lines,
82	  so the page can fold them later.
83	- **Frontend: lo-fi variants first, hi-fi only when asked.** UI work
84	  proposes two or more lo-fi variants before any code. Build each as a
85	  throwaway mock in plain HTML, grey boxes and system text, no styling, in a
86	  scratch directory, and capture it with the browser tool. `splates attach`
87	  each and put it under its own choice, lettered A, B, C in order, one image
88	  each. Then read the answer:
89	  - A pick means build it. Hi-fi is never required: most changes land from
90	    the lo-fi pick.
91	  - A pick with words, or a request for more, means another round of lo-fi.
92	  - When the user asks to see the look rather than the layout, make hi-fi
93	    mocks (real styling, real components or the app's own CSS) and work them
94	    with the user until one is approved. Never build hi-fi mocks unasked.
95	
96	To capture, use the browser tool when you have one; otherwise headless
97	Chrome from Bash (`"/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome"
98	--headless=new --screenshot=out.png --window-size=720,480 file:///…`), or any
99	installed Chromium. A text sketch in a code block is no screenshot: capture one.
100	`splates attach` works only from a task worktree or a conversation
101	(`$SPLATES_CONVERSATION`). With neither, `splates add` the task the proposal
102	would become first, as every proposal needs one, and attach from its worktree
103	(keeping the scratch files outside it).
104	
105	Every visual is a before and after, side by side or one under the other, so
106	the change is what the eye finds. The before is the code as it is now: a D2
107	diagram of today's flow, drawn from the code (find it with `git grep`, not a truncated file listing; when there truly is none, draw today's flow as the user described it and say so), a real screenshot of today's screen (a new screen has
108	no before, so say so). The after is the intent: the proposed diagram, or the
109	lo-fi mock. Label each `Before` and `After`, and label a mock as a mock.
110	
111	End your turn after it; ask nothing else beside it.
112	
113	The `splates server` page shows a proposal as a questions card headed by it, each
114	call with a `(chosen)` choice already answered with it. Once every call is
115	answered and the user has changed none of your choices, its button approves,
116	sending `[SPLATES APPROVE]`, then the answer to each call you chose nothing
117	for, quoted as any answer is. That, or a reply
118	of "approve", means go ahead as proposed, taking in each answer, every call
119	not quoted as you chose it, after `splates add` when no task is under way. A
120	reply without it, as the card sends once the user picks another choice,
121	changes a call or writes anything else, answers what it quotes: take that
122	in and propose again.
123	
124	**Approve carries the pictures into the task.** On approval, before any code,
125	make sure the task's `SPLATES.md` holds what was approved: `## Before` and
126	`## After` with the proposal's short summary, and `## Verification` with its attached mock images inline
127	(`![what](/abs/path.png)`, the stored paths `splates attach` printed, not the
128	scratch captures), each answered call folded in. When the proposal was written
129	before the task existed, `splates add` it now and write the sections then, with
130	the same images, so they are the record that *Expected* later pairs with *As
131	built* (see SPLATES.md in the skill). Never leave the pictures only in the
132	reply, and never re-capture them.

1	# splates.config.ts
2	
3	What a project's `splates.config.ts`, at the root of its repository, can set.
4	Read this before you read or change it, or when the user asks what splates
5	can be set to do. Change it in a task like any other code: it is checked in
6	and shared by everyone on the project, and a running `splates server` picks
7	up a change once it lands, without a restart. Never write a secret, a
8	personal host or an email address into it.
9	
10	The file default-exports only what differs from the defaults, typed by a
11	type-only import, so it loads without splates installed:
12	
13	```ts
14	import type { ConfigFile } from "@stringsync/splates/config";
15	
16	export default {
17		postCheckout: "bun install",
18		preMerge: "bun test",
19	} satisfies ConfigFile;
20	```
21	
22	A config wrapping its export in `defineConfig(...)` is from before
23	`ConfigFile`; `splates update` rewrites it. Every command below runs via
24	`sh -c`. When an option here is missing or seems out of date, the `Config`
25	interface in `@stringsync/splates/config` (`packages/server/config/config.ts`
26	in the splates repository) documents each one, and its defaults are in
27	`load.ts` beside it.
28	
29	## Branches and worktrees
30	
31	| Option         | Default                               | What it sets                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
32	| -------------- | ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
33	| `trunk`        | the branch `origin/HEAD` names, else `main` | The branch tasks start from and land on.                                                                                                                                                                        |
34	| `remote`       | `null` (`"origin"` on a deployed server with an SSH origin) | The git remote each task's branch is pushed to as `splates/<task>`, so a task outlives the machine; with one, trunk is the remote's and only the server pushes it. `null` pushes nothing.                  |
35	| `worktreeRoot` | `<repo>-splates.noindex`, beside the repo | The directory holding a worktree per task. The `.noindex` keeps Spotlight from indexing it.                                                                                                                     |
36	| `platform`     | `null`                                | `"linux"`, `"macos"` or `"windows"` for a project that builds only there: its tasks wait for a worker on it.                                                                                                       |
37	
38	## Commands around a merge
39	
40	| Option         | Default | When it runs                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
41	| -------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
42	| `postCheckout` | `null`  | In each new worktree `splates add` makes, as `"bun install"`.                                                                                                                                                                              |
43	| `postRewrite`  | `null`  | After `merge` rebases, before `preMerge`, since a rebase can bring a dependency the worktree never installed; a ship runs it too, in the main tree before its command, and a landing that changes a lockfile runs it there after it lands.                                                                                                                              |
44	| `queueLoad`    | `1.5`   | Load per core that holds starts when CPU is also at least 80%. CPU or memory at 90% also holds starts; they resume after ten seconds below 80% CPU and 85% memory, checked every five seconds. Tasks the user starts by hand are never held. `null` never holds. |
45	| `preLock`      | `null`  | After the first rebase, before the merge waits for the premerge lock: a quick check that needs neither the lock nor the cores. A nonzero exit fails the gate. `preMerge` then gets `$SPLATES_CHECKED`, the commit it passed on, to skip what it covered. |
46	| `preMerge`     | `null`  | The last gate, after the rebase: a nonzero exit leaves the base untouched. `null` merges on a clean rebase alone. Writing a JUnit report to `$SPLATES_TEST_REPORT` (`bun test --reporter=junit --reporter-outfile="$SPLATES_TEST_REPORT"`) queues a task for each test over 5 seconds, and from Bun charges an attempt only for failures the task caused. |
47	| `ship`         | `null`  | What the ship runner runs from the root to ship the project: publish its packages at their next version and tag the release on trunk, or, for a deploy target (see `legacyShips`), put it out with no version. `null` never ships it. Only the user ships. |
48	| `afterBump` | `null` | A command for consumers to run after installing this project’s new versions, such as `"bunx @stringsync/splates refresh"`. Retained for ship-step adoption; the old cascade no longer runs bump tasks. |
49	| `legacyShips` (read as `ships` when absent) | `null` | `{ name: { ship, dependencies?: ["other-target"] } }`: commands implementing the core/legacy-ship ShipCommand contract (`plan --json`, `status --json`, and run). `dependencies` names targets that ship, or are already current, before this one (the page pulls them in and locks them, and leaves out one already current), forming a tree; unknown names and cycles are refused. `needs` and `after` are refused: rename them to `dependencies`. The command owns identity, inputs, steps, source paths and live evidence. Unsupported commands are refused with adoption guidance. Versioned plans declare step packages; deploy plans declare repository-relative literal source paths for unshipped counts. With none, there are no ship targets. |
50	
51	## Task events
52	
53	`on` maps a task event to a shell command, run in the main tree:
54	`on: { "task.done": "./notify-team" }`. The events are `task.created`,
55	`task.updated`, `task.queued`, `task.started`, `task.done` and
56	`task.dropped`. The command gets the event in `$SPLATES_EVENT`, its tasks'
57	numbers in `$SPLATES_TASKS`, comma separated, and a started task's name in
58	`$SPLATES_TASK`. Shell commands only: a hook that runs an agent spends one
59	person's tokens, so each person adds their own from the Setup page or
60	`splates hook add`.
61	
62	## Projects
63	
64	A repository can hold several projects. Splates keeps the two apart: the
65	**repository** is the git side, one trunk, remote, set of worktrees, merge
66	lock and `postCheckout`/`postRewrite` hooks, all set once in this file; a
67	**project** is only a set of paths inside it. Declare them here, in the
68	checked-in file, so every agent and worker sees the same boundaries; a
69	project cannot declare itself from a folder of its own.
70	
71	```ts
72	export default {
73		projects: {
74			wren: ["wren/**"],
75			vet: ["vet/**", "docs/vet.md"],
76		},
77		shared: ["package.json", "bun.lock", "bin/**"],
78	} satisfies ConfigFile;
79	```
80	
81	- `projects` maps a slug to the globs, relative to the repository root, that
82	  project owns. A path belongs to the first project whose glob matches it.
83	  A slug may instead map to `{ paths: [...], ship, afterBump }`:
84	  the project's own `ship` and `afterBump` (`null` included),
85	  each falling back to the repository's when left out.
86	- `shared` lists paths every project uses, such as the lockfile or root
87	  tooling. A change to them counts against no project.
88	- A path neither claims belongs to no project.
89	- With no `projects`, the repository is one project covering every path,
90	  named after the repository's folder, and `shared` is ignored. Single-repo
91	  users change nothing. To pick the name, declare `projects: { name: ["**"] }`.
92	- A config is refused when it loads if a slug is empty, a project owns no
93	  paths, a glob is absolute or climbs out with `..`, or two projects overlap.
94	  Overlap is judged by the literal directories before each glob's first
95	  wildcard, so `core/**` and `core/packages/x/**` clash, and so do `a/*.ts`
96	  and `a/b/**` though they could not match one path. Give each project its own
97	  top-level folder. A slug listed twice is a duplicate object key, which
98	  TypeScript refuses.
99	
100	Each task records the project it changes: `splates add` and `splates task
101	add` take `--project <slug>`, else the project whose folder they run in, else
102	the only project; a task started from a queued one inherits its project.
103	
104	In code, `new Scopes(config, repoName).of(path)` answers
105	`{ kind: "project", slug }`, `{ kind: "shared" }` or `{ kind: "none" }`
106	(`packages/server/config/scopes.ts`).
107	
108	## Limits
109	
110	| Option                         | Default        | What it caps                                                                                         |
111	| ------------------------------ | -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
112	| `mergeRetryCount`              | `5`            | Failed merge attempts before only the user's `splates retry` allows another.                       |
113	| `mergeConflictCount`           | `10`           | Conflicted rebases before the same, counted apart from failed gates.                                 |
114	| `leaseStalenessMs`             | `90000`        | How long since a task's last heartbeat before its lease is up for grabs.                             |
115	| `taskStalenessMs`              | 30 days        | How long a queued task waits before `merge` offers it for removal rather than recommending it.       |
116	| `removedCapacity`              | `50`           | Removed task names kept, so `remove` can say "already removed".                                      |
117	| `finishedCapacity`             | `500`          | Finished tasks kept, with their `SPLATES.md`, for the Tasks page.                                    |
118	| `logCapacity`                  | `1000`         | Events the log holds before it is moved aside and a fresh one starts.                                |
119	| `attachmentCapacity`           | 100 MiB        | Bytes of `splates attach` files one task may hold.                                                   |
120	| `artifactFileCapacity`         | 50 MiB         | Bytes one artifact may be.                                                                           |
121	| `artifactConversationCapacity` | 250 MiB        | Bytes of artifacts one conversation may keep ([artifacts.md](artifacts.md)).                         |
122	| `artifactProjectCapacity`      | 2 GiB          | Bytes of artifacts every conversation in the project may keep together.                              |
123	
124	Byte and millisecond options take plain numbers, as `100 * 1024 * 1024`.
125	
126	## Server and page
127	
128	| Option           | Default                 | What it sets                                                                                                                                                                                           |
129	| ---------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
130	| `tunnel`         | `null` (`cloudflared`)  | A `TunnelProvider` of the project's own for `splates server --tunnel`: [setup.md](setup.md), under the tunnel of their own.                                                                            |
131	| `replica`        | `null`                  | Where the server keeps a copy of the project's records, to move them to another machine: `{ provider: "s3", endpoint, bucket }`, whose keys the Creds page asks for, or `{ provider: "dir", path }` ([transfer.md](transfer.md)). |
132	| `evals`          | `null` (no Evals page)  | `{ results, list?, run?, plan? }`: where eval batches land for the Evals page and the commands its run card lists, prices and starts them with (`docs/evals.md` in the splates repository).            |
133	| `dictationWords` | `[]`                    | Words the composer's mic spells as written for everyone on the project, as `["wren", "vet"]`; each person adds their own on the Setup page.                                                       |
134	| `projects`       | `null` (the repository is one project) | `{ slug: ["globs/**"] }`: the projects inside the repository, each the paths it owns. See [Projects](#projects). |
135	| `shared`         | `[]`                    | Path globs that count against no project, such as the root `package.json`. See [Projects](#projects). |
136	| `tags`           | `null` (any tag, none required) | `{ allowed?: [...], required?: boolean, colors?: { <tag>: <color> } }`: free labels that group tasks without making them projects; ships, queues and the merge gate ignore them. Tasks take them with `--tag <name>` (repeatable or a comma list; lowercase with dashes) on `splates add`, `task add`, `task defer` and `task update` (`--remove-tag` drops one), and `list` and `task list` filter by `--tag`. With `allowed`, an unknown tag is refused, naming the allowed ones, and a task added from inside a folder named for an allowed tag gets it by default. With `required: true`, a new task with no tag is refused. Only new and updated tasks are checked; existing tasks stay valid untagged. `colors` tints a tag's chips on the page, one of red, orange, amber, green, teal, blue, indigo, violet, pink or gray; a tag without one gets a neutral chip. |
137	| `vet`            | `"vet/bin/vet"`         | The command the Budget page runs `budgets` with, from the repo's root.                                                                                                                              |
